programs.name: Ethiopia Data Use Partnership (DUP) – African Health Initiative Phase 2
programs.administrator: JSI Research & Training Institute, with the Ethiopia Federal Ministry of Health
programs.description: National program to strengthen health-information use and digital health systems in Ethiopia's primary health care. Gates led; DDF gave a supplemental grant.
programs.caveats: Gates is named by both JSI and DDF. Only a DDF page names the Global Fund, and that page was seen only as a search snippet.

programs.name: Mozambique Integrated District Evidence to Action (IDEA) – African Health Initiative Phase 2
programs.administrator: Health Alliance International (DDF grant); University of Washington (NIH grant); Mozambique Ministry of Health; Beira Operations Research Center
programs.description: District-led audit-and-feedback program to reduce newborn deaths. DDF funded the program and NIH/NICHD funded the study of its spread.
programs.caveats: The two grants ran in parallel rather than as one pooled fund. NIH money went to a US university; that it reached Mozambique is inferred from the project's sites and Mozambican co-investigator.
programs.us_work_evidence: Work in Mozambique (NIH grant paid to a US university for the Mozambique study)

programs.name: Ghana CHPS+ – African Health Initiative Phase 2 (follow-on to GEHIP)
programs.administrator: Ghana Health Service; Navrongo Health Research Centre; Columbia University
programs.description: Scale-up of Ghana's community-based primary health care (CHPS) model from three pilot districts to three regions.
programs.caveats: KOICA funded a parallel CHPS+ scale-up in the Upper East Region. JICA is named in only one search snippet. A paper also lists USAID, Gavi, the World Bank, Samsung and the Global Fund as supporters of Ghana's wider strategy; they are not counted as co-funders here.

programs.name: NOHARM MTD trial – hydroxyurea for children with sickle cell anemia
programs.administrator: Cincinnati Children's; Makerere University / Mulago Hospital (Kampala); Indiana University
programs.ddf_contribution: Not disclosed (Innovations in Clinical Research Award)
programs.description: Randomized trial in Uganda showing that raising the hydroxyurea dose cut clinical events in children with sickle cell anemia (NEJM, 2020).
programs.caveats: Cincinnati Children's money may have stayed in the US (in the earlier trial it paid for the US data center). Addmedica donated the drug, which is in-kind, not money.
programs.us_work_evidence: Trial in Uganda (some co-funder money may have stayed in the US)

programs.name: Energy Foundation – US and China clean energy (DDCF Climate Change Initiative)
programs.administrator: Energy Foundation; China Sustainable Energy Program (now Energy Foundation China, Beijing)
programs.description: DDCF's largest climate grant, to build clean-energy markets in the US and China, including green-building work in China.
programs.caveats: Other foundations funded the same recipient and its China program in the same years. No source describes a formal pooled fund with set shares.
programs.us_work_evidence: Grant built clean-energy markets in the US and China

programs.name: French-American Jazz Exchange (FAJE)
programs.administrator: Chamber Music America (from 2006); Mid Atlantic Arts Foundation (US side, from c.2010); FACE Foundation / Albertine Foundation (French side)
programs.description: Grants for joint French and US jazz projects, with concerts and recordings in both countries.
programs.caveats: French musicians are named grantees, but no source shows how the money was split between countries.
programs.us_work_evidence: Concerts and recordings in both countries; US side run by Mid Atlantic Arts

programs.name: FUSED – French-U.S. Exchange in Dance
programs.administrator: NEFA National Dance Project; Cultural Services of the French Embassy; FACE Foundation
programs.description: Two-way dance residencies and tours. French presenters hosted US artists and US presenters hosted French companies.
programs.caveats: Money going to France is inferred from projects at French venues; no source names who was paid.
programs.us_work_evidence: Two-way: US presenters hosted French companies

programs.name: Performing Americas Program (PAP)
programs.administrator: National Performance Network (NPN) with La RED (Red de Promotores Culturales de Latinoamérica y el Caribe)
programs.description: Two-way touring and residency exchange between US presenters and artists and those in Latin America and the Caribbean.
programs.caveats: Later NPN pages name DDF as the only funder. Puerto Rico also took part but is a US territory, so it is not counted.
programs.us_work_evidence: Two-way: US presenters and artists took part

programs.name: Center Stage (borderline)
programs.administrator: New England Foundation for the Arts (producer); Lisa Booth Management
programs.description: State Department cultural diplomacy program that brought foreign ensembles on US tours.
programs.caveats: Co-funding is well documented, but the money mainly paid for touring inside the US. Ensembles' home countries are listed, but no source confirms fees were paid abroad.
programs.us_work_evidence: Money mainly paid for tours inside the US
